title: Maneuver
description: One option a character with superiority dice can spend them on. A maneuver is the smallest unit of the superiority system: a character learns a fixed number of them, and using one normally costs a die out of a pool that refreshes on a rest. Two things therefore have to be answerable without reading the prose, because a player answers them every round: which list the maneuver comes from, and what using it costs. Both are fields here rather than sentences in the description.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this maneuver. Derived from the name once and never reused, so saved characters keep resolving after a rename.

name.description: Display name, usually a verb phrase for what the maneuver does: Disarming Blow, Goading Attack, Tactical Assessment. An upgrade of an existing maneuver keeps the base name and adds a parenthesised tier, as in "Administer Aid (Improved)"; that spelling is load-bearing, because it is how the printed lists show that the two are one maneuver at two tiers.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this maneuver was published in, matching a document of the source content type. Values present in the archive are phb and ec.

contentSet.description: Whether this maneuver belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.

maneuverType.description: Which of the three maneuver lists this one is drawn from. This is not flavour: a class feature grants access to a named list, so the type decides who may learn the maneuver at all. General maneuvers are open to everyone with superiority dice; physical and mental ones are gated on the feature that grants them, which is why Parry (Improved) exists purely to move Parry from one list to the other.

superiorityDice.description: How many superiority dice using this maneuver spends. Almost every maneuver spends exactly one. Zero is the meaningful case and there are two kinds of it: an upgrade that changes how an already-paid-for maneuver behaves rather than being used on its own, and the handful whose printed text has the player roll a superiority die without expending it. Recording the cost as a number rather than inferring it from the prose is what lets a character sheet subtract from the pool, and what lets the print pipeline set the cost in the margin the way the books do.

prerequisite.description: What a character must already have to learn this maneuver, as printed: a skill proficiency ("Proficiency in Medicine"), a casting ability ("The ability to cast force powers"), a companion, or another maneuver named as "<Name> maneuver". Omit when anyone with superiority dice may learn it.

improves.description: Name of the maneuver this one is an upgrade of, for the tiered maneuvers whose text reads "When you use your <base> maneuver, ...". Recorded separately from prerequisite because the two answer different questions and do not always agree: Administer Aid (Greater) improves Administer Aid, but its prerequisite is Administer Aid (Improved), the tier in between. A reader needs the chain; a character builder needs the gate.

description.description: Markdown rules text in second person, describing what happens when the maneuver is used. The archived corpus writes the action cost into the opening clause of this text — "As an action, you can expend a superiority die" — rather than into a field of its own, and that phrasing is kept verbatim rather than parsed, because the same maneuver can be usable at several action costs depending on which tiers of it a character has taken.
